evidence: CVE.org record API https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-77639 reports state PUBLISHED and describes remote concatenated gzip/zlib members bypassing the compression-bomb check, affecting Tor from 0.3.1.1-alpha before 0.4.9.9.

At dec2222c65159fc21ca5e40a3e85cb3f821454bd, src/feature/dirclient/dirclient.c passes the received directory HTTP body from dir_client_decompress_response_body() to tor_uncompress(); src/lib/compress/compress.c recreates the backend state after TOR_COMPRESS_DONE when input remains, while src/lib/compress/compress_zlib.c keeps bomb counters inside that recreated state.

GitLab first-party patch https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/core/tor/-/commit/880fb3e3a9aba21c0b36aa4aa5659432e90eb827.patch shows 880fb3e3a9aba21c0b36aa4aa5659432e90eb827 first adding tor_compress_impl(), including the concatenated-member branch that frees and recreates stream without a cumulative ratio check.

git ls-tree 91dd4a00f7d4891e24187a849933547128aeeb9f gives src/common/compress.c blob 38b818457351d26f241c5be69c0c451f91127e97 and src/common/compress_zlib.c blob faa179f7c141c9b9ff5a56e70db892f9ba3675a5; direct inspection finds no tor_compress_impl() in that parent.

The parent src/common/compress_zlib.c handles a following member by inflateEnd()/inflateInit2(), but its allocation-growth gate calls tor_compress_is_compression_bomb(in_len, out_size) with whole-call input and cumulative output allocation, so the vulnerable per-member counter reset is absent.

880fb3e3a9aba21c0b36aa4aa5659432e90eb827 is an ordinary one-parent commit, not a merge or revert; its first-party patch directly adds the smallest surviving public implementation containing the flaw, and its commit object names no squash members or finer public commits.

bug_semantics: A directory server controls the compressed HTTP response body consumed by Tor's directory client. For gzip/zlib data containing multiple concatenated members, tor_compress_impl() accepts each TOR_COMPRESS_DONE boundary and creates a fresh backend state. The zlib backend's input_so_far/output_so_far bomb detector is state-local, so many individually sub-threshold, highly expanding members reset the detector at every boundary and collectively consume excessive CPU/memory without rejection.
flaw_origin: Commit 880fb3e3a9aba21c0b36aa4aa5659432e90eb827 replaced backend-specific one-shot decompressors with a shared streaming front end and first wrote the vulnerable free/recreate path without a cumulative cross-member ratio check. Its immediate parent handled concatenated zlib/gzip members while retaining a whole-call input and cumulative output allocation check, so this is a semantic regression rather than a move-only carrier.
